primitives.name: Convex-Conjugate Market Maker
primitives.verbatim_quote: - **Design rule via conjugate duality:** `C(q) = sup_{x∈Π} x·q - R(x)` (1) for strictly convex R with domain Π = H(ρ(O)); prices `∇C(q) = argmax_{x∈Π} x·q - R(x)`.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'C(q)': "Market maker's cumulative cost at state q (dimensionless)", 'x': "Traders' belief vector (dimensionless)", 'q': 'State vector representing outstanding trades (dimensionless)', 'R(x)': 'Dual potential function (dimensionless)', 'Π': 'Feasible belief set (dimensionless)'}
primitives.assumptions: Strict convexity of R; compact, convex feasible set Π; linear payoff structure ρ(O); no-arbitrage condition.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Non-differentiability of C(q) when q lies on the boundary of Π; unbounded losses occur if Π is too small.

layer2.mapping: The convex-conjugate market maker is mathematically equivalent to the Logarithmic Market Score Rule (LMSR) when R is the negative entropy and Π is the probability simplex. This isomorphism bridges prediction markets to online convex optimization.
layer2.telemetry: Observed bid-ask spreads track the inverse of the smallest eigenvalue of ∇²C(q); realized losses are verified against the Bregman divergence D_R(·,·).
